title: Full n-Bit SPRP Security from an n-Bit-State Primitive
summary: With state and output restricted to n bits, achieving full n-bit SPRP security from a single tweakable block cipher remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Can an SPRP based on an $n$-bit-state primitive achieve full $n$-bit security?

scope.domain: Beyond-birthday SPRP security from a single tweakable block cipher with n-bit state and output.
assumptions: The tweak length is at least the primitive state size.
parameters: n: the primitive state and output size and the target full-security level
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether full n-bit SPRP security is achievable in this model.

citations.label: ZCZ – Achieving n-bit SPRP Security with a Minimal Number of Tweakable-Block-Cipher Calls

progress.summary: The source presents an explicit feasibility question about obtaining full n-bit security from primitives with n-bit state size in the beyond-birthday SPRP setting.
citation_labels: Ritam Bhaumik et al., ZCZ – Achieving n-bit SPRP Security with a Minimal Number of Tweakable-Block-Cipher Calls
